findings.description: The `pup map` catch repeats the body of `refusedUnsandboxed()` (instanceof UndeclaredSandboxError → refuse(error.message), else rethrow), so the CLI now has two refusal mechanisms for one error that a future change to the refusal format must keep in sync; a shared wrapper in the style of `refuseMalformedSpec` (returning undefined on refusal) would fold both and drop the `let nodes: ReturnType<typeof buildCodeMap>` + try/catch shape.

The adapter layer imports `UndeclaredSandboxError` only to special-case it in its catch; any future adapter that wraps `runGateChild` errors will need the same rethrow, so the 'don't wrap the sandbox refusal' rule may belong in a shared capability helper (next to `failureSummary`) once a second caller appears.

The new `const mode = sandboxMode();` in `runGateChild` shadows the module-level cached probe `let mode: SandboxMode | undefined;` (line 151); a distinct name such as `current` avoids the reader confusing the two.

In-code docs lag the new passthrough: the `DECLARATION_VAR` JSDoc still says it is the only place the declaration is read, and the `GateChildOptions.gateEnv` doc doesn't mention that `runGateChild` now adds `PUP_SANDBOX` to the passthrough itself when pup runs in declared-vm; only decision 78's addendum records it.
Comment typo: "so the declaration is its too" should read "is its, too" (or "is theirs too").

"a vitest default waits for a Linux CI job" is cryptic: say what default (a vitest-level `PUP_SANDBOX` default) is deferred and why, e.g. "a vitest-level default for PUP_SANDBOX is deferred until a Linux CI job exists".

The test comment restates the test title and its `not.toContain('Custom adapter')` assertion; its only WHY (depGraph is a gate child) is already implied by the name, so it can be cut to one line or removed.

The new test adds another inline copy of the `process.platform` override-and-restore block, while `src/cli/index.test.ts` already uses an `onPlatform` helper; this widens the duplication flagged in the prior round.
